decision_conditions: The applicant has failed to demonstrate, through the submission of a parking stress survey or other robust evidence, that sufficient capacity exists within the surrounding highway network to accommodate the parking demand arising from the proposed intensification of the site from a dwellinghouse to an eight-person Sui Generis House in Multiple Occupation. Given the site's Public Transport Accessibility Level (PTAL) of 2, the loss of the existing garage parking provision and the likely increase in parking demand associated with the proposed use, the development would exacerbate on-street parking pressure within the surrounding area. In the absence of sufficient evidence demonstrating that adequate parking capacity exists to accommodate the development, the proposal is contrary to Policies T2, T3, T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies DMD45, DMD47 and DMD48 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed development fails to provide adequate, secure, convenient and accessible cycle parking facilities for future occupiers. The proposed cycle storage would require bicycles to be manoeuvred through the dwelling and does not provide a safe or convenient means of access. Furthermore, the site is unable to accommodate policy-compliant cycle parking without compromising either the remaining parking provision or the character of the streetscene. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies T2, T3, T5 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), Policies CP24 and CP25 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD45, DMD47 and DMD48 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed first-floor rear extension, by virtue of its siting, scale, bulk, projection and proximity to the shared boundary with No. 261 Carterhatch Road, would result in an unacceptable loss of outlook, increased sense of enclosure and reduction in daylight to neighbouring habitable accommodation and private amenity space. The proposal would therefore cause material harm to the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, contrary to Policies D3, D4, D6 and D8 of the London Plan (2021), Policies CP4 and CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD8, DMD10 and DMD11 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed first-floor rear extension, by reason of its scale, depth, width, bulk and projection beyond the established rear building line, would appear as an unduly dominant and visually intrusive addition that fails to respond appropriately to the prevailing pattern of development in this section of Carterhatch Road. The proposal would disrupt the consistent rear form of the surrounding semi-detached properties and would therefore cause harm to the character and appearance of the host dwelling and wider area, contrary to Policies D3, D4 and D8 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), and Policies DMD6, DMD8, DMD11 and DMD37 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The proposed 8-person Sui Generis HMO would represent an over-intensive form of occupation that the application site is unable to accommodate satisfactorily. The cumulative requirements associated with the intensified use, including increased refuse provision, cycle parking demands, higher levels of activity and the need for substantial built form additions to facilitate the accommodation, would result in a form of development that would be out of keeping with the established pattern and character of development within Carterhatch Road. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMD5(d), DMD6, DMD8 and DMD37 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), Policies D3, D4 and D8 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and the design objectives of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).
